summary: William H. Nienhauser, Jr. is a sinologist who studied at Indiana University, the Defense Language Institute, Cleveland State, and Bonn, working under Irving Yucheng Lo and Friedrich Alexander Bischoff. He became full professor (1983) and Halls-Bascom Professor (1995) at Wisconsin-Madison.
William Homan Thorpe studied at Jesus College, Cambridge (1921–1925). He held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1932 to 1969 and taught John Crook.

William James was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who studied at Plymouth College and Harvard (including an 1869 medical degree). He taught at Harvard University from 1872, serving as assistant professor of physiology, philosophy, and finally professor (1885).

William Jones was an Indologist and linguist educated at Harrow, Oxford, and Middle Temple, studying under Mirza I'tisam-ud-Din, Ramachandra, and Ramalocana. He served as Chief Justice of Bengal's Supreme Court (1783) and founded The Asiatic Society (1784).

William L. Ames works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He earned an M.S. at Caltech and a Ph.D. at the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg and Collett Cox. He held posts at Washington, CIIS, and JFK University.

William M. Bodiford works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at Kansas and Yale (Ph.D. under Stanley Weinstein), with training at Komazawa and Tsukuba. He taught at Davidson and Iowa before joining UCLA circa 1992.

William M. Gorvine specializes in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned his B.A. from Connecticut College and an M.A. and Ph.D. from the University of Virginia, where he was supervised by David F. Germano.

William Magee works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his Ph.D. under Jeffrey Hopkins at the University of Virginia, where he was attested as professor in 1992, and later held posts at Dharma Drum and Chung-Hwa Institute.
William P. Chu is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned an M.A. at the University of California, Los Angeles in 2006, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Robert Buswell.

William Price was a scholar in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He taught oriental languages at Netherstone House Seminary and served as Professor of Hindústaní at Fort William College from circa 1813 to 1830.

William R. Hutchison was a scholar of religious studies and history. He studied at Oxford and Yale, holding posts at Yale, Hunter College, Wisconsin-Madison, and American University, before teaching at Harvard University from 1968.

William R. LaFleur specialized in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Calvin, Michigan, and Chicago (Ph.D. 1973), he held posts at Princeton, UCLA, and the University of Pennsylvania, where he became E. Dale Saunders Professor.

William Rainey Harper was a linguist educated at Muskingum and Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He taught at Denison, Baptist Union Seminary, and Yale, before serving as president of the University of Chicago (1891–1906) and Bradley University (1897–1899).

William Roxburgh was an Indologist educated at Edinburgh and Aberdeen under John Hope and Alexander Monro. He served in the Madras Medical Service, directed the Samalkot Garden (1781), and was superintendent of the Indian Botanic Garden (1793).

William S. Waldron is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his Ph.D. at Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota, Ichijo Ogawa, and Seiki Miyashita, and has held posts at Otani University and Middlebury College.

William S.-Y. Wang is a linguist and sinologist who studied at Columbia and Michigan. He held long-term posts as professor at UC Berkeley (1966–1994), City University of Hong Kong, and Chair Professor at Hong Kong Polytechnic University.

William Stede was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He served as an editor for the Pali Text Society (circa 1916–1925) and held an academic post at SOAS, University of London, from 1928 to 1949.

William Van Gordon is a researcher in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Attested in 2015, he founded the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research and worked as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University.

William Ward was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Ewood Hall Theological Academy under John Fawcett in 1797. He served as a missionary at the Serampore Mission (1800–1823) and co-founded Serampore College in 1818.

William Wilson Hunter was a historian and Indologist who studied at Glasgow, Paris, and Bonn. He served in the Indian Civil Service (1861–1887), became Vice-Chancellor of Calcutta University (1886), and vice-president of the Royal Asiatic Society (1890–1900).
